title: Requirement extraction from project files (foundational)
description: The resolver reads project manifests, import statements, and lockfiles to build the raw requirement list. Static import scanning catches undeclared dependencies that manifests miss, using the language's own parser. The extracted list is the resolver's ground truth about what the project needs. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import ast
src = 'import requests\nimport numpy as np\n'
tree = ast.parse(src)
imports = {n.names[0].name.split('.')[0] for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.Import)}
print('detected imports:', sorted(imports))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Dependency Resolver practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Version constraint solving by backtracking (foundational)
description: Version constraints are solved with backtracking search: pick the most constrained package, try its newest allowed version, and recurse. When a choice leads to a conflict, the solver backtracks to the last decision point and tries the next version. Backtracking is complete for the small constraint problems typical of dependency resolution. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Dependency Resolver practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

t: Conflict diagnosis with minimal culprit set (foundational)
title: Conflict diagnosis with minimal culprit set (foundational)
description: When no solution exists, the resolver finds a minimal set of conflicting constraints by removing constraints one at a time until solving succeeds. The removed set is the diagnosis: these specific requirements cannot all hold at once. Reporting the minimal culprit set turns 'resolution failed' into an actionable fix list. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
reqs = ['a>=2.0', 'a<1.5', 'b==1.0']
print('conflict candidates:', [r for r in reqs if r.startswith('a')])
print('diagnosis: a>=2.0 and a<1.5 cannot both hold -> relax one')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Dependency Resolver practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Lockfile generation for reproducibility (foundational)
description: The solved versions are written to a lockfile pinning every transitive dependency to an exact version with its content hash. The lockfile makes installs reproducible: the same file installs the same tree on any machine. Lockfiles are checked into version control alongside the project. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Dependency Resolver practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Platform filtering of candidates (foundational)
description: Candidate versions are filtered by platform tags: operating system, architecture, and Python version. A version that cannot install on the target platform is excluded before solving, not discovered after. Platform filtering prevents the classic failure of resolving beautifully on one machine and breaking on another. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
cands = [{'v': '1.0', 'py': '>=3.9'}, {'v': '0.9', 'py': '>=3.7'}]
py_ver = (3, 11)
ok = [c for c in cands if py_ver >= tuple(map(int, c['py'].lstrip('>=').split('.')))]
print('platform-compatible:', [c['v'] for c in ok])
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Dependency Resolver practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
